features.name: Brainstem / Project Lifecycle
features.description: Recursive rhythm pattern: prepare → execute → integrate → gate at every scale
features.plan: Define the end-to-end project lifecycle that the Attention Scheduler will drive. Not implementation — design specification. What happens at each beat, which components fire, what data flows.
features.notes:
The brainstem has three responsibilities, not one. (1) RHYTHM: recursive four-phase pattern (prepare/execute/integrate/gate) that nests at every scale. Each phase maps to a brain region. (2) HOMEOSTASIS: continuous monitoring of vital signs (WM load, prediction accuracy, context capacity, learning health, weight volatility) with reflex-level responses. Context management is breathing — evict/load without PFC involvement. (3) REST: load-triggered consolidation cycles (NE=0) using the same rhythm pattern. Crystallize episodes, prune memory, decay connections, recalibrate predictions, settle weights. Rest happens when the system needs it, not on a schedule. Replan cascade: drift→replan→re-manifest→diagnostics→escalate. Diagnostic event bus foundation complete (steps 1-5 of spec). Steps 6-8 (gate/pipeline/learning instrumentation) are incremental.

features.name: Thalamus
features.description: Context routing layer — each consumer gets exactly what it needs
features.plan: Build the central relay that assembles context for each consumer. Dual-layer API: Layer 1 categorical getters (stable, any consumer composes from these) + Layer 2 convenience composers (encode selection intelligence for known consumers). Key principle: contextual extraction, not concatenation. Generous inclusion with clear organization for v1 — filter more aggressively later once we see what the system actually uses.
features.notes: Brainstem owns the Thalamus (same pattern as WM and HomeostasisMonitor). Constructed with persistent sources (WM, PNS), updated with per-project sources (intent, taste) when a run starts. Passed to rhythm definition factories. Future sources (hippocampus, cerebellum, basal ganglia) plug in via optional fields — no registration ceremony. Taste dissolution and intent slicing are future enhancements once the routing infrastructure exists.

features.name: Attention Scheduler
features.description: Stateless decision function — reads signals, returns one action. Replaces naive nextReadyTask() in task-dispatch.prepare().
features.plan: Not a loop driver (brainstem handles that). A stateless decision function called by task-dispatch.prepare(). Reads WM, task graph, vitals. Priority cascade: complete > perseveration > drift-replan > drift-escalate > open-questions > cratering > rest > dispatch > deadlock. features.name: Sensory Cortex Loop
features.description: Make the sensory cortex rhythm loop: senses consult → build-cycle runs → senses evaluate → gate checks improvement potential → re-consult. The same intelligence that plans also evaluates, and evaluation feeds back into the next plan.
features.notes: Core insight: the senses are both the planners (consultation) and the evaluators (receptors). Previously they planned once and never re-engaged. Outer sensory-cortex loop (3 iterations) handles guidance-level changes via re-consultation.
